slides.header: 1. Income Statement
slides.full_text:
1. Income Statement
Covers a PERIOD of time (e.g., the year ended Dec 31, 2025)
Shows whether the company generated a profit by matching revenues 
earned against the expenses incurred to earn them.
• Revenue ,  what was earned from customers
• Cost of Goods Sold → Gross Profit
• Operating Expenses → EBIT (Operating Income)
• Interest Expense & T ax → Net Income
• Net Income flows into the Statement of Changes in Equity
2. Statement of Changes in Equity
Covers a PERIOD of time, rolling equity forward
Shows how and why total shareholders' equity moved from the 
beginning to the end of the period.
• Beginning Equity balance
• + Net Income (from the Income Statement)
• − Dividends Paid; +/− share issuances or buybacks
• = Ending Equity balance → feeds the Balance Sheet
3. Balance Sheet (or Statement of Financial Position)
A SNAPSHOT at one point in time (e.g., as of Dec 31, 2025)
Shows what the company owns, what it owes, and what belongs to 
shareholders ,  at that single moment.
• Assets = Liabilities + Equity (always)
• Current vs. non-current assets and liabilities
• Cash balance ties to the Statement of Cash Flows
• Equity balance ties to the Statement of Changes in Equity
4. Statement of Cash Flows
Covers a PERIOD of time, reconciling cash actually received and paid
Explains why cash went up or down ,  separating operating, investing, 
and financing activity so readers can see cash quality.
• Operating (CFO) ,  cash from core business, starts from Net Income
• Investing (CFI) ,  capex, acquisitions, asset sales
• Financing (CFF) ,  debt, equity, dividends
• Ending cash ties directly to Cash on the Balance Sheet

What to Remember from Today
The four statements aren't independent ,  net income and cash both trace back to the same 
balance sheet, through different paths.
Accrual accounting matches revenue with the effort that generated it ,  and is exactly why net 
income and cash flow can diverge.
The real substance of an annual report lives in the notes and the auditor's opinion, not the 
glossy front pages.
Strategy analysis comes first because you cannot judge a number without understanding the 
business behind it.
Porter's Five Forces gives a structured way to assess whether an industry's economics favor or 
work against a company.

Net income and cash differ by design ,  not by error.
Classify every flow as operating, investing, or financing, then read the sign pattern first.
Direct and indirect methods must reconcile ,  use that as your accuracy check.
Free cash flow (CFO − Capex) is the foundation of DCF valuation, coming in Weeks 13-14.

slides.full_text:
C L A S S A C T I V I T Y
CFO Reconstruction
Purpose: This is not a copying exercise ,  for most groups, the reconciliation you're building here doesn't 
exist anywhere in your company's published filings, and even when it does, deriving it independently is 
the actual skill being taught, not the final number .
How to: Build your reconciliation independently, without looking at your company's own reconciliation 
(most groups won't have one to look at anyway). Then compare your result to the actual reported CFO 
figure.
Why this matters: In Week 13 (Forecasting), you'll build a projected cash flow statement for your 
company ,  one that hasn't happened yet, with no published figure to check against. If you haven't 
practiced deriving a cash flow statement from an income statement and balance sheet by hand, that task 
becomes far harder than it needs to be. Today is deliberately building that muscle while you still have a 
real answer to check yourself against.

Common-size statements make companies of different sizes, and years, genuinely comparable.
ROE is one number hiding three stories: margin, turnover, and leverage.
The real skill is judgment: which driver moved, and is that change sustainable?
A ratio is only meaningful in comparison ,  to trend, or to the right sector peers.
Choose peers by business model, not just size or industry label.

value

Maturity profile The portion due within 12 months must be covered by cash or refinancing, which links to the current ratio from Week 6

The Five-Step Model (Recap)
The critical judgment throughout: when does control actually transfer to the customer?

Step Question it answers Where judgment appears
1. Identify the contract Is there an enforceable agreement? Verbal or implied contracts can still count

milestone1_strategy: BUSINESS AND INDUSTRY ANALYSIS
Porter's Five Forces PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk
Financial Statement Analysis
Magister Manajemen Universitas Klabat
Group 4
Ramschie Fagly | Ruitan Anggreini | Rompas Galatia
Final Group 4 FSA Write-Up
Executive Summary

GoTo operates across Indonesia's digital economy through On-Demand Services, Financial Technology, and e-commerce-related services. Its scale, integrated ecosystem, and technology provide important advantages, but strong competition, price-sensitive users, substitutes, and regulatory demands keep profitability and execution central to the company's position.
Source: GoTo Annual Report 2025, pp. 8, 76-84, 147-152.
1. Company and Industry Overview
1.1 Company Overview

PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk is an Indonesian technology company and digital ecosystem formed from Gojek and Tokopedia. It connects consumers, driver-partners, merchants, sellers, and financial-service users through On-Demand Services, Financial Technology, and e-commerce-related services. Gojek provides mobility, food delivery, and logistics, while GoPay provides payments, lending, and merchant solutions; Tokopedia remains connected through e-commerce service fees after deconsolidation. Because these services share users, merchants, payments, data, and technology, GoTo operates as one ecosystem rather than a single-product company. In 2025, GoTo reported Rp18.3 trillion in net revenue, with On-Demand Services as the largest contributor, followed by Financial Technology and e-commerce.
Source: GoTo Annual Report 2025, pp. 8, 63, 76-84, 150-155.
Key 2025 Financial and Operating Context
Source: GoTo Annual Report 2025, pp. 14-18, 41, 155-158.
1.2 Industry Overview

GoTo operates mainly in on-demand services, e-commerce, and financial technology, industries structured around digital platforms, network effects, and scale. Larger networks of users, merchants, and driver-partners make a platform more useful and allow technology and operating costs to be spread across more transactions. These markets are still growing: in 2025 Indonesia's digital economy reached about USD99 billion in GMV, digital-payment GTV reached about USD538 billion, digital lending about USD13 billion, and transport and food-delivery GMV about USD10 billion.
Source: GoTo Annual Report 2025, p. 147.

Competition remains strong because customers have many alternatives and relatively low switching costs. Gojek competes with platforms such as Grab, Maxim, and inDrive; GoFood competes with GrabFood and ShopeeFood; and GoPay competes with DANA, ShopeePay, OVO, banks, and other payment providers. Price, promotions, convenience, service quality, regulation, technology, cybersecurity, and platform scale are therefore central to industry performance.
Source: Meilina (2025); Ahdiat (2026); Ridwan (2026); GoTo Annual Report 2025, pp. 40, 46, 147 and 168-169.
2. Porter's Five Forces Analysis
2.1 Threat of New Entrants

GoTo's Threat of New Entrants is rated Low to Moderate. New companies can enter individual digital segments, but matching GoTo's scale requires substantial technology, marketing, customer acquisition, regulatory compliance, and networks of users, merchants, driver-partners, and business partners. In 2025, GoTo had 66 million Annual Transacting Users, more than 6.4 million registered merchants, and more than 3 million registered driver-partners, giving it network effects and operating experience that are difficult to reproduce quickly. Payment and lending activities also require regulatory capability. However, specialized entrants can still target a single service, so the threat is not fully Low. For GoTo, this means its ecosystem and scale provide protection, but continuous improvement in technology, pricing, service, and customer experience remains necessary.
Source: GoTo Annual Report 2025, pp. 8, 63, 76-84 and 180-183.
2.2 Bargaining Power of Suppliers

GoTo's Bargaining Power of Suppliers is rated Low. The company has formal supplier-selection and development policies, transparent procurement procedures, and a Vendor Code of Conduct designed to secure goods and services at competitive prices and good quality. No purchases from any third-party supplier exceeded 10% of consolidated net revenue in 2025, and GoTo's digital-services model is less dependent on imported raw materials than a manufacturing business. Specialized technology vendors and foreign-exchange exposure can still create some switching or cost pressure, but there is no evidence of a dominant supplier that can dictate GoTo's terms. This gives GoTo a relatively strong position to control cost, quality, and supply continuity.
Source: GoTo Annual Report 2025, p. 325; Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 26.
2.3 Bargaining Power of Buyers

GoTo's Bargaining Power of Buyers is rated Medium. Customers are price-sensitive and can shift activity when another platform offers a better price, promotion, or service experience, so GoTo must remain competitive on affordability, quality, speed, convenience, and personalization. Its promotions include cashback, shipping subsidies, discounts, and other incentives, while its strategy also distinguishes between mass-market users seeking affordable and predictable solutions and more affluent users prioritizing quality, speed, and convenience. Buyer power is not High because GoTo's user base is very large and fragmented: in 2025 it had 66 million Annual Transacting Users, more than 6.4 million merchants, and about 3 million driver-partners, with no single customer accounting for 10% or more of consolidated net revenue. Buyers therefore influence GoTo's strategy collectively, but no individual buyer can determine its terms.
Source: GoTo Annual Report 2025, pp. 8, 56, 148, 152 and 168-169; Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 25.
2.4 Threat of Substitute Products or Services

GoTo's Threat of Substitutes is rated Medium because customers can satisfy the same needs without using the corresponding GoTo service. Public transportation can replace some ride-hailing trips, dining in can replace food delivery, and cards, bank transfers, other e-wallets, or account-to-account payments can replace some GoPay transactions. Switching friction is relatively low, although the Annual Report does not publish a numerical switching-cost measure. GoTo reduces this pressure by integrating alternatives into its ecosystem: GoTransit combines commuter rail and GoRide, GoDineIn keeps GoTo involved when customers eat at restaurants, and GoPay supports several payment and funding methods. Because digital payments and transport and food delivery were still growing in 2025, substitutes are meaningful but are not eliminating demand, so GoTo must compete on convenience, value, and ecosystem integration rather than only against direct platform rivals.
Source: GoTo Annual Report 2025, pp. 77-82 and 147.
2.5 Competitive Rivalry Among Existing Firms

GoTo's Competitive Rivalry is rated High and is the strongest force in the analysis. Gojek, GoFood, and GoPay compete with established platforms that offer closely overlapping services, while users can compare prices, promotions, and service quality and can use several applications at the same time. GoTo itself identifies intensifying digital-economy competition and pricing competition as important risks. Banks need an adapted DuPont model. A bank's 'revenue' (interest and fee income) is itself a return on its main asset (loans), so the standard Net Margin × Asset Turnover pairing becomes definitionally circular. Group 4 ,  Fagly Ramschie, Anggreini Ruitan and Galatia Rompas

Milestone 3 reviews GoTo’s 2024-2025 accounting quality. All amounts are in Rp million. Our source is the 2025 consolidated financial statements, issued in March 2026 (PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk [GoTo], 2026). Page references below identify pages in that financial statements PDF.
(a) Accounting quality red flags
Investment values and recoverability

Tokopedia and Bank Jago had carrying values of 7,432,326 and 2,894,921 in 2025. Together they represented 22.57% of GoTo’s assets and included goodwill of 2,003,559. GoTo also held 1,668,574 of Level 3 other investments. These are separate from Tokopedia. Repeated impairment and fair-value losses make the valuation assumptions worth reviewing (GoTo, 2026, p. 17; Notes 14-15, pp. 100-103; Evidence B).
Revenue recognition and related parties

GoTo’s judgments about gross versus net revenue and customer incentives affect reported revenue and margins. Related-party revenue rose to 1,306,110, or 7.13% of 2025 revenue. These are areas for review, rather than proof of misstatement. GoTo also states that no single customer contributed 10% or more of revenue (GoTo, 2026, Note 25, p. 129; Evidence C). Section (d) explains the policies.
Optional scenario with a 20% reduction

We use this scenario to ask what would happen if the two investments lost 20% of their recorded value. Each Rp100 would fall to Rp80. The 20% assumption comes from our Week 10 group assignment. Tokopedia’s starting value already includes goodwill, so we do not add it again.

The assumed loss totals 1,820,180, leaving 7,280,720 in these investments. This would reduce GoTo’s total assets by 3.98%, before tax. This shows that lower investment values could noticeably reduce GoTo’s reported assets, so their valuation assumptions deserve attention. However, the financial statements do not establish that a 20% reduction is needed or likely. Evidence B provides the starting balances.
(b) Accrual ratios for two years

We use year-end total assets consistently for both years. Both ratios are negative because the accounting loss is larger than the operating cash outflow in 2024, and GoTo reports a loss alongside positive operating cash flow in 2025. The narrower gap does not by itself establish stronger earnings quality. Noncash charges and working-capital movements also affect it (GoTo, 2026, pp. 15, 17, 21).

Year-end total assets. GoTo (2026), statement of financial position, p. 15. The column heading and total are excerpts from the same page.
Connection to Milestone 2

Milestone 2 reported an improving net margin, from −34.4% in 2024 to −8.2% in 2025. The accrual comparison supports reviewing that improvement alongside cash flow, rather than relying on the smaller loss alone (Group 4, Milestone 2). Evidence A, D and E contain the underlying figures.
(c) Analytical adjustments

We keep GoTo’s reported result as the main measure. The comparison below removes selected valuation charges to show their effect on profit before tax. We then separately remove the share of associate and joint-venture results to examine their contribution. These comparisons are not GoTo’s reported earnings or a forecast of recurring profit.

In 2024 we add back the associate and joint-venture loss of 2,305,125. In 2025 we subtract their profit of 249,100. This explains the opposite signs in the second-last row. The 2025 calculation is 84,062 less 249,100, giving a loss of 165,038.
Inputs to the adjustments. GoTo (2026), income statement, p. 17. The column heading and rows are excerpts from the same page.

Impairment losses occurred in both years, so excluding them can overstate sustainable performance. The Level 3 loss is included within fair-value movements and is not added back again. These charges appear below operating profit, leaving the reported 2025 operating loss of 378,254 unchanged. Tax effects are not estimated (GoTo, 2026, pp. 17, 103).
(d) Revenue recognition policy and judgment

For GOJEK platform transactions, GoTo generally acts as an agent because it arranges the sale or trip without controlling the goods or driver services. It records its service fee when the sale or trip is completed. The principal-versus-agent judgment affects whether revenue is presented gross or net (GoTo, 2026, Note 2s, pp. 66-67).

E-commerce fees and customer incentives

E-commerce consultancy fees are recognised over time, using Tokopedia’s gross merchandise value multiplied by the agreed fee percentage. This requires reliable transaction data and evidence that the service is provided over time (GoTo, 2026, Note 2s, p. 71).

Customer incentives reduce revenue when GoTo receives no distinct good or service in return, or cannot reliably measure its value. Incentives exceeding the related expected revenue become selling and marketing expenses. Applying these rules affects both revenue and margins (GoTo, 2026, Note 2s, p. 71; Evidence C).

Milestone 2 found 15.3% revenue growth and a gross-margin increase from 53.4% to 57.7% in 2025. Revenue presentation therefore matters when interpreting the improvement. (a) Executive Summary

This report presents an integrated financial statement analysis and valuation of PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) for 2023 to 2025, connecting our findings from Milestones 1 through 4 into an actionable decision for an equity investor. GoTo is Indonesia's largest digital ecosystem across On Demand Services (Gojek), Financial Technology (GoPay), and e-commerce service fees (from Tokopedia). However, our analysis shows that scale and user reach have not yet translated into sustainable economic profit.

1. Industry and Strategic Position (Milestone 1): GoTo operates in a high rivalry industry where customers have low switching costs and easily compare prices across Grab, Maxim, inDrive, ShopeeFood, OVO, and DANA. GoTo uses a mix of cost leadership and differentiation, which forces it to spend heavily on promotions (Rp 3.09 trillion in 2025 sales and marketing) and product development (Rp 2.15 trillion) just to defend its market share.

2. Accounting Quality and Red Flags (Milestone 3): GoTo remains unprofitable under Indonesian financial accounting standards (PSAK), reporting consolidated net losses of Rp 90,519 billion in 2023, Rp 5,465 billion in 2024, and Rp 1,502 billion in 2025. Total equity fell from Rp 35,720 billion in 2023 to Rp 28,712 billion in 2025 because of Rp 215.3 trillion in accumulated losses. Furthermore, 22.57% of GoTo's assets sit in Tokopedia (Rp 7,432 billion) and Bank Jago (Rp 2,895 billion) investments, alongside Rp 1,669 billion of Level 3 investments that carry impairment risk. Operating cash flow was only Rp 307 billion in 2025, covering just 26.0% of its Rp 1,182 billion capital expenditure.

3. Financial Ratios and DuPont Analysis (Milestone 2): While operating loss narrowed from -69.5% of revenue in 2023 to -2.1% in 2025, Return on Equity (ROE) remained negative in all three years (-253.4% in 2023, -18.0% in 2024, and -5.2% in 2025). Debt doubled in 2025 from Rp 3,820 billion to Rp 7,743 billion (raising Debt to Equity from 0.13x to 0.27x). GoTo's survival is currently supported by its Rp 21,755 billion cash balance (current ratio of 2.73x), which acts as a buffer while operations attempt to break even.

4. Three Year Forecast and Breakeven (Milestone 4): In our Base Case forecast anchored on GoTo's 2023 to 2025 historical averages (11.4% revenue growth, 41.1% COGS, 78.5% cash operating expenses, and 16.3% capex), GoTo stays below breakeven in all three forecast years (2026F to 2028F), posting annual EBIT losses of Rp 4,003 billion to Rp 4,967 billion and burning its cash balance down from Rp 21,755 billion in 2025 to just Rp 968 billion by 2028F. GoTo only breaks even if management freezes fixed operating expenses in rupiah terms instead of letting costs grow with revenue.

5. Valuation and Recommendation (Assignment 14): WACC 7.76%, Ke 8.45%, DCF -Rp121.1/share and residual income -Rp75.1/share retain the submitted assumptions. The revised Grab-only P/B benchmark is Rp91.0/share. At the assignment reference price of Rp25, our SELL / AVOID recommendation follows the milestone cash-burn forecast and negative economic profit, rather than an average of incompatible valuation methods.

PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk connects 66 million Annual Transacting Users, more than 6.4 million merchants, and over 3 million driver partners in Indonesia. After deconsolidating Tokopedia in early 2024 (retaining a 24.99% associate stake), GoTo now relies on two active operating engines: On Demand Services (Gojek mobility, GoFood delivery, and logistics, which generated Rp 12,361 billion in 2025 revenue) and Financial Technology (GoPay payments and consumer loans, which grew 74.1% to Rp 5,191 billion in 2025), alongside Rp 820 billion in e-commerce service fees from Tokopedia.
